about: Asking a portal for a playable URL, and telling a useless answer from a good one.
notes: Arguments are the helper's name and its arguments: linkAttempts, stripLinkPrefix or hasBlankStreamId.

A portal matches `create_link` against what it stored, and portals disagree about what that is. There is no way to tell which from outside, so the forms are tried in turn — and the order matters: the stored form first, because most portals want exactly what they sent.
hasBlankStreamId is why the attempts are needed at all. A portal that did not recognise the cmd answers 200 with a URL that names no channel. It looks like success until ffmpeg opens it.

cases.name: an empty stream parameter is a refusal dressed as a URL
a whitespace-only parameter counts as empty
a real stream id is not blank
a URL with no such parameter at all is not blank
cases.why: Absent is not empty. Plenty of portals answer with a path and no query, and treating that as a refusal would reject every one of them.
